guest.name: 村井さん
guest.role: Owner of {村井電器|むらいでんき}, the electronics and phone-repair shop on the shopping street

context: Thursday morning: アルちゃん drops his phone in the orchard and finds it an hour later in a puddle, dead. He still hasn't answered レン's first message, so he rushes to {村井電器|むらいでんき} on the shopping street.
scene: Your phone spent the morning in a puddle and won't turn on. You still owe レン a reply. You run to the repair shop.

phrases.jp: スマホを{落として|おとして|to drop|4}、{画面|がめん|screen|4}が{割れちゃった|われちゃった|to crack, break|4}。
phrases.en: I dropped my phone and cracked the screen.
phrases.note: {割|わ}れる = crack (glass, screens). ちゃった adds 'oops'.

phrases.jp: {急に|きゅうに|suddenly|4}{電源|でんげん|power (switch)|3}が{入らなく|はいらなく}なっちゃったんです。
phrases.en: Suddenly it won't turn on any more.
phrases.note: {電源|でんげん}が{入|はい}る = to turn on. Works at any phone or repair counter.

phrases.jp: {約束|やくそく}したから、{行かない|いかない}わけにはいかないよ。
phrases.en: I promised, so I have to go.
phrases.note: Double negative = 'I have no choice but to go'.

phrases.jp: {仕事中|しごとちゅう}なので、{電話|でんわ}に{出る|でる}わけにはいかないんです。
phrases.en: I'm at work, so I can't take the call.
phrases.note: {電話|でんわ}に{出|で}る = answer the phone. The reason is a rule, not ability.

phrases.jp: {やばい||uh-oh; bad|4}、{充電|じゅうでん|charging; battery|4}が{切れそう|きれそう|to run out|4}…。
phrases.en: Uh-oh, my battery's about to die.
phrases.note: {充電|じゅうでん}が{切|き}れる = the battery dies.

dialogue_setting: {村井電器|むらいでんき}, a small electronics shop on the shopping street, late Thursday morning.

dialogue.speaker: 村井さん
dialogue.jp: いらっしゃい。あれ、スマホの{画面|がめん|screen|4}、{真っ暗|まっくら|pitch dark|3}だね。どうしたの？
dialogue.en: Welcome. Oh, your phone's screen is completely black. What happened?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {今朝|けさ}、{畑|はたけ|field, orchard|4}で{落として|おとして|to drop|4}、{一時間|いちじかん}も{探した|さがした|to look for|4}んです。
dialogue.en: This morning I dropped it in the orchard and spent a whole hour looking for it.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: やっと{見つけたら|みつけたら|to find|4}、{水たまり|みずたまり|puddle|3}の{中|なか}で…。それから{電源|でんげん|power (switch)|3}が{入らない|はいらない}んです。
dialogue.en: When I finally found it, it was in a puddle… Since then it won't turn on.

dialogue.speaker: 村井さん
dialogue.jp: あー、{水没|すいぼつ|water damage, sunk|2}か。{今|いま}すぐ{充電|じゅうでん|charging (a battery)|4}するわけにはいかないね。{一晩|ひとばん|one night|3}{乾かそう|かわかそう|to dry (something)|3}。
dialogue.en: Ah, water damage. I can't charge it right away. Let's dry it overnight.
dialogue.note: {水没|すいぼつ} = 'sunk': shop talk for any phone that got wet.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: でも、{今日|きょう}は{返事|へんじ|reply|4}しないわけにはいかないんです。{待ってる|まってる}{人|ひと}がいて…。
dialogue.en: But I really have to reply today. Someone's waiting…

dialogue.speaker: 村井さん
dialogue.jp: じゃあ、{明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}{取りに|とりに}{来て|きて}。{待ってる|まってる}{人|ひと}には、{後で|あとで}{謝れば|あやまれば|to apologise|4}いいよ。
dialogue.en: Then come and pick it up tomorrow morning. Just apologise to whoever's waiting later.

listening.intro: As you leave the shop, {村井|むらい}さん calls after you.

lines.jp: {明日|あした}は10{時|じ}に{開ける|あける}からね。それまで{充電|じゅうでん|charging|4}しちゃだめだよ！
lines.en: I open at 10 tomorrow. Don't charge it before then!

grammar.form: verb (dictionary): + わけにはいかない ({休|やす}むわけにはいかない, {充電|じゅうでん}するわけにはいかない) · verb ない: + わけにはいかない = must ({行|い}かないわけにはいかない) · polite: わけにはいきません ({出|で}るわけにはいきません)
grammar.explanation: You can't do something because of duty, rules or conscience, not because it's impossible. With ない it becomes 'I have no choice but to': {行|い}かないわけにはいかない. Don't use it for ability: 'I can't swim' is {泳|およ}げない.
mark: 返事しないわけにはいかない
充電するわけにはいかない
行かないわけにはいかない
出るわけにはいかない
断るわけにはいかない
寝るわけにはいかない

examples.jp: {先輩|せんぱい|senior (at work, school)|3}に{誘われたら|さそわれたら|to invite|3}、{断る|ことわる|to refuse|3}わけにはいかない。
examples.en: If a senior invites you, you can't really say no.

examples.jp: {明日|あした}は{試験|しけん}だから、{今夜|こんや}は{寝る|ねる}わけにはいかない。
examples.en: The exam is tomorrow, so I can't go to sleep tonight.

quiz.question: {熱|ねつ}があるけど、{今日|きょう}は{大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}だから、{休む|やすむ}＿＿。
quiz.en: I have a fever, but today's meeting is important, so I can't take the day off.
quiz.explain: Duty stops you, so わけにはいかない. わけがない = 'no way', わけではない = 'it's not that'.

quiz_more.question: {親友|しんゆう|best friend|3}の{結婚式|けっこんしき|wedding|3}だから、{行かない|いかない}＿＿。
quiz_more.en: It's my best friend's wedding, so I have to go.
quiz_more.explain: The fixed form is わけにはいかない: ない-form + it means 'I must'.

quiz_more.question: {子供|こども}のころから{水|みず}が{怖くて|こわくて}、{今|いま}も＿＿。
quiz_more.en: I've been scared of water since I was a kid, and I still can't swim.
options: 泳ぐわけにはいかない
泳がないわけにはいかない
quiz_more.explain: This is ability, not duty, so use the potential form {泳|およ}げない.

kanji.where: The sign in the window of {村井電器|むらいでんき}: スマホ{修理|しゅうり} {受付中|うけつけちゅう} (smartphone repairs taken).
kanji.breakdown: {修理|しゅうり}: 修 mend, put right + 理 order, logic → putting something back in working order: repair.
kanji.related: {修理|しゅうり}に{出|だ}す = send for repair; {修理代|しゅうりだい} = repair fee.

tip.title: Phones and water
tip.body: In shop talk a phone that got wet is {水没|すいぼつ} ('sunk'), even if it only fell in a puddle. Many Japanese phones are {防水|ぼうすい} (waterproof) because people use them in the bath. If one dies anyway, don't charge it: dry it first.

challenge.hint: How do you say 'that's so embarrassing'?
challenge.prompt: That evening {恵子|けいこ}さん tells the family LINE group. {颯太|そうた} replies: 「{水|みず}たまりで{一時間|いちじかん}もスマホ{探してた|さがしてた|to look for|4}の？{ウケる||hilarious (slang)|3}ｗ」 She hands you her phone. You're embarrassed. Which sticker?
challenge.explanation: {恥|は}ずかしい… is how you laugh at yourself after a silly mistake. すげー！ and やった！ cheer good news, and おおきに is Kansai 'thanks', which makes no sense as a reply here.

vocab.note: {画|が} picture + {面|めん} surface. {画面|がめん}が{割|わ}れる = the screen cracks.
{真|ま}っ = completely + {暗|くら}い. Also {真|ま}っ{白|しろ}, {真|ま}っ{赤|か}.
You drop it: {落|お}とす. It falls: {落|お}ちる.
For something lost or wanted: {仕事|しごと}を{探|さが}す = job hunting.
水 water + たまる to collect.
{電源|でんげん}を{入|い}れる / {切|き}る = switch on / off.
{充|じゅう} fill + {電|でん} electricity. {充電器|じゅうでんき} = charger.
{一晩中|ひとばんじゅう} = all night long.
You dry it: {乾|かわ}かす. It dries: {乾|かわ}く. {髪|かみ}を{乾|かわ}かす.
{人|ひと}に{謝|あやま}る. The polite noun is {謝罪|しゃざい}.

kanji_study.parts: 日 sun radical + 音 sound → the sun is gone and you only have sounds to go on: dark.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 晴 (clear weather): both have 日 on the left, but 晴 has 青 blue, 暗 has 音 sound.

kanji_study.parts: 扌 hand radical + 罙 (a hole 穴 with a tree 木) → a hand reaching deep into a hole: search.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 深 (deep): same right side, but 深 has 氵 water, 探 has 扌 hand.

extras.title: Phone trouble
extras.intro: What you'll say at a phone shop, or to a friend with a charger.

items.jp: スマホが{フリーズした||to freeze (device)|3}。
items.note: Also {固|かた}まった: 'it set hard'.

items.jp: そろそろ{機種変|きしゅへん|switching to a new phone|3}しようかな。
items.en: Maybe it's time for a new phone.
items.note: Short for {機種変更|きしゅへんこう}, what shops call it.

items.jp: {充電器|じゅうでんき|charger|3}、{貸して|かして}くれない？
items.en: Can you lend me a charger?
items.note: The most-asked favour at any guesthouse.

items.jp: Wi-Fiのパスワード、{教えて|おしえて}もらえますか。
items.en: Could you tell me the Wi-Fi password?
items.note: Often on a card next to the router.

extras.title: Telling a mishap in order
extras.title_jp: {失敗|しっぱい}の{話し方|はなしかた}
extras.intro: Three linkers that make a story of what went wrong.

items.jp: {最初|さいしょ}は、{全然|ぜんぜん}{気づかなかった|きづかなかった|to notice|4}。
items.en: At first I didn't notice at all.

items.jp: そしたら、{急に|きゅうに|suddenly|4}{変|へん}な{音|おと}がして…。
items.en: And then suddenly there was a strange noise…
items.note: そしたら = casual そうしたら, 'and then'.

items.jp: {結局|けっきょく|in the end|4}、{全部|ぜんぶ}{やり直し|やりなおし|doing over, redo|3}だった。
items.en: In the end I had to redo everything.
